Supernova census explorer

Seven years of the ZTF Bright Transient Survey: every classified supernova that peaked brighter than 18.5 mag. Project L2 of the Astrophysics Project Atlas (all data public; see the project README).

The zoo: how bright, and for how long

Duration = time above half of peak brightness (rest frame). Click a point to inspect it; click a family to show or hide it. Absolute magnitudes are not corrected for dust in the host galaxy.

Click a supernova

Light curves (ZTF g and r alert photometry via ALeRCE) are available for every Type II and the best-observed few of each other class.

Survey simulator: magnitude-limited vs per volume

Top: what the survey finds at that depth (classified events, weighted for classification completeness). Below: per unit volume (1/Vmax, brighter than M = −14), and the Lick Observatory Supernova Search's volume-limited census (Li et al. 2011). Ib/c includes Ic-BL, Ibn, Icn; II includes IIb, IIn.

Missing stars: the red supergiant problem

– of the progenitors in the sample would have been born above 18 M☉, and the chance of finding none would be –.

Salpeter IMF between 8 M☉ and the chosen mass; the sample is Davies & Beasor (2018)'s 24 Type II-P/L supernovae with progenitor detections or limits. None was more massive than ~18–20 M☉. With measurement errors and luminosities instead of masses the tension is milder: a sample like this shows nothing brighter than the brightest seen of the time (see Fig. 10).
